content.main_review:
This paper presents a multi-hop reasoning framework for forecasting future links on temporal KG. The novelty of this paper is that the proposed method designs three indicators to characterize the temploral KG and reasoning path. Overall, it is an interesting work. 

Strengths:
1. The idea is clear and the solution is somewhat novel. 
2. The paper is well written and the results are good. 


Weakness:
1. The results on YAGO are not convincing. For example, the results for TTransE, TA-DisMult, TA-TransE and CyGnet are lower than 15% on Hits@10. But the Re-Net, zERTR and IMR obtain more than 60% on Hits@10. It is very strange. In fact, the dataset of YAGO in Table 1 hould not be used any more.  The authors should use the YAGO described in CyGNet (Zhu et al., 2020), DBKGE (Liao et al., 2021) and TITer (Sun et al., 2021). 
Zhu et al., 2020. Learning from history: Modeling temporal knowledge graphs with sequential copy-generation networks. AAAI 2021.
Liao et al., 2021. Learning Dynamic Embeddings for Temporal  Knowledge Graphs. WSDM 2021.
Sun et al., 2021. TimeTraveler: Reinforcement Learning for Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting. EMNLP 2021. 

2. The authors should compare with the latest studies DBKGE (Liao et al., 2021) and TITer (Sun et al., 2021). As you know, DBKGE has published on Feb, 2021, nearly 6 months ago before the deadline of ICRL 2022. 

3. The codes are not availabel, it is difficult for others to re-produce the results. 

I suggest the authors provide the results on YAGO described in CyGNet (Zhu et al., 2020), DBKGE (Liao et al., 2021) and TITer (Sun et al., 2021) and compare with DBKGE (Liao et al., 2021) and TITer (Sun et al., 2021) in the response phase.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, authors propose a novel framework called IMR(Interpretable Multi-hop Reasoning), which implements temporal knowledge graph forecasting by transforming reasoning into multi-step question answering. Considering the choice of multiple reasoning paths, the authors propose three scores to rank various paths.
content.main_review:
Strengths
1. The model improves over other temporal forecasting models by integrating paths of multiple hops and has good interpretability. The authors also provide a detailed case study to elucidate this algorithm and its advantage.

Weaknesses
1. What are the advantages of this method compared with methods based on reinforcement learning, like [1]? The score function (e.g., formula 5) designed in the paper can be understood as a greedy method, which preferentially selects the path whose destination is closer to the goal. Is such a greedy algorithm too simple and limited compared to RL method? 
2. This article attempts to solve the multi-hop reasoning problem on dynamic KG. However, the method of dealing with dynamic KG only includes the existing time-aware exponentially weighted sampling method. What are the innovations in this paper on this task?

Some detailed question:
1. What is remaining subject and relation in the model used for? I don’t see this symbol again in the paper. 
2. Why only sum rp1 and rp2 in Ep. 6? Here should be the sum of r on the entire path.
I did not understand how to determine whether to stop, that is, to determine that the current end has been reached.
3. The wording is confusing. For example, the e in Eq.7 is called query. I think what author want to express is the entity? There are many examples of this, which make it difficult to read the paper.

[1] Lin, X. V., Socher, R., & Xiong, C. (2018). Multi-Hop Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Reward Shaping. In Proceedings of the 2018 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (pp. 3243-3253).

content.title: Response to Reviewer fqts
content.comment:
Answer for Weakness 1：

Thanks for the valuable comments, which promoted our understanding of the model.
The reinforcement learning models are black-box models, which cannot explain the basis of judgment. Moreover, reinforcement learning utilizes rewards, which is essentially a measure of the matching degree between tails and the question. This end-to-end design is essentially one of the Question Matching Degree in IMR, unexplainable and complicated.
IMR is the first to design indicators from the perspective of actual semantic, so we select the basic TransE as the basis for IMR. The modeling of triples in TransE is elementary, so the formulas of indicators are simple. Compared with the complex greedy algorithm, it is natural to take the design of IMR as too simple.
Although the design of IMR is simple, it achieves better performance than complex reinforcement learning models. Besides, we are conducting interpretable indicator designs based on other complex and more expressive models. The indicators based on these models will be more complex, and the performance will be better. This part of the work is in progress.
The main contribution of this paper is the interpretable multi-step reasoning framework from actual semantic. Although the current design based on the elementary model is relatively simple, the design routes are valuable. Even having complex scoring functions, the departure of reinforcement learning models belongs to the Question Matching Degree in IMR. We should not compare the complexity of IMR with that of reinforcement learning models.

Answer for Weakness 2：

Thanks for your comments. We have considered the temporal dynamics of temporal KG.
First of all, we have tried a new sampling strategy, and our attempt is more in line with reality. However, the experiments are not good, so they are not shown in this paper.
Besides, the dynamic consideration for temporal KGs mainly lies in Path Confidence. The same entities with different timestamps are likely to have different attributes. When the attribute difference between entities is significant, the next-hop path searching cannot be performed based on the same entity. Therefore, Path Confidence is to measure the changes in attributes due to different timestamps.
In addition, based on the embeddings in xERTR, IMR proposes an extra component of embedding for the same entity with different timestamps. This will be introduced in Appendix A.1 in details. In response to overfitting, we also introduced regularization on continuity.

Answer for Question 1:

It is our negligence in not unifying the description for the same variables in the paper, which confused your reading. We feel very sorry.
These remaining subjects and relations will be used in Section 4.2: Entity pruning and path sorting. It appears in the following equations.

$f_{ac}^i = {\left\| r_{q_-i} \right\|}_p$

As shown in Equation 6, Answer Completing Level calculates the P norm for the remaining relation of the question.

${f_{pc}^i} = \left\| e_{q_-i}- e_i^{t_i} \right\|_p$

As shown in Equation 7, the remaining subject of the question is applied for the calculation of path confidence.
We have unified the description and symbols in Section 4.



Answer for Question 2:

Thanks again for discovering the fault in the paper. The equation should be:

$f_{ac}^i = {\left\| r_q-r_{p1}-r_{p2}-r_{p3}-...-r_{pi} \right\| }_p$ .
The closer these three indicators are to 0, the better the path.
IMR does not need stop conditions. We set limitations on the maximum hop for the complexity. When the combination of the three indicators reaches the minimum, we believe that the inference path reaches the current optimal solution.
We have modified the equation and explained optimization goals in Section 4.

Answer for Question 3:

We are sorry for the confusion caused by an ununiform description for variables.
We take the task of link prediction ${\left( {e_s},{r_q},?,{t_q} \right)}$ as a query or a question. We used to name the question after the query.
There may be some misunderstandings about paper. Equation 7 is

${f_{pc}^i} = \left\| {e_{q_-i}}-e_i^{{t_i}} \right\|_p$

Where $e_{q_-i}$ represents the remaining subject of the question updated by paths of the length $i$, and $e_i^{t_i}$ represents the tail reasoned by the $i$-hop paths.
Questions include subjects and relations. Questions after updating based on path searching are called the remaining questions. The remaining question also includes the remaining relation and the remaining subject. The remaining relation and the remaining subject will be utilized to obtain the Answer Completing Level and the Path Confidence, respectively.
We unified the description and the representation of variables. Besides, we checked and corrected the normative and consistency of other variables in the paper.

We are sorry for our mistake in writing the paper, and thanks again for your careful reading and valuable comments.

display_title: Official Review of Paper892 by Reviewer 5a2j

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper presents an interpretable multi-hop reasoning approach for event prediction on temporal graphs (Graphs where each triplet of entities and relations has an associated timestamp). The task is ‘temporal KG forecasting’, where past historical facts are utilized to predict the future triplets. 

Inspired from multi-hop question answering, interpretability in the paper is defined as finding the most appropriate path where the combination of relations is equivalent to the query’s relation. 
For scoring and choosing the path, three indicators are proposed: Question matching degree to find the answer entity, which has the least distance from the query entity, Answer completing level to find the combination of paths which is the distance of the relations in the path to that of the query, Path confidence to measure the validity of each path.  
The paper includes empirical results and comparisons on ICEWS and YAGO, along with an ablation study for the three indicators.
content.main_review:
Strength

The strength of the paper lies in the ability to provide a basis for path comparison. It can measure the paths of different hops and utilize them for reasoning. The problem handled is important for interpretability in temporal KGs. The inspiration taken from multi-hop QA is interesting and the proposed approach can be extended into further directions. 

Weakness

1) In section 5.3 of ‘Case studies and Interpretability’, the authors show an example for one of the queries - (John Kerry, Make a visit, ?, 7536) and draw conclusions: ‘answer completing level can effectively indicate how well the combination of path relations equals to the relation of the query’, ‘ time distance between the paths and the query is gradually increasing, which means that the reliability of the paths gradually decreases.’ All these conclusions have been drawn from just one example from the dataset. It would make more sense to see in how many cases do these hold true. The first part is difficult to compute for all data samples but the second point could be shown for multiple samples and checked if the claim still holds true.

2) ‘In the further analysis of paths, 97% of entities inferred by 3-hop paths are included in tails predicted by paths with one and two hops. Nearly no new positive samples are obtained, and numerous new negative samples are imported’ - This brings up the question of combining a multihop approach as opposed to an approach where the hops are fixed. In the experiments section, we are essentially combining paths that are 1 and 2 hops away. How would that be useful in terms of interpretability as opposed to when we have results from another fixed hop approach like ClusTer? Since we can just go till 2 hops the complexity of the problem reduces. How do the authors justify this approach to reasoning? Of course, using a richer dataset could be one of the ways but no conclusion can be drawn from the datasets used in the experiments.

3) The standard deviations are not reported for the runs. Hence it is difficult to form conclusions especially for table 3 where the numbers are much close to each other. 

4) How do the authors justify the combination of the three indicators giving worse results for YAGO dataset in table 3? How does this worse performance affect the interpretability?

5) ‘ IMR can always obtain the best inference performance by combining these three indicators.’ This is not evident from table 3 where the combination of all on Yago gives a worse performance.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The authors propose an interesting approach and problem statement but the experiments do not fully justify the claims in the paper. Having variance for multiple runs, justification of why using three indicators reduces the performance and showing interpretability of multiple samples instead of just one would help in better evaluation. 

Here are some areas which would help in significantly improving the paper quality - 

1) Indicating the variance of multiple runs in the tables 2 and 3 along with just reporting the point accuracy would help in making the claims stronger.

2) Supporting the claims made in the paper by relating to the numbers in table 3  would add credibility to the claims made. 

3) The effectiveness of the method would be highlighted by making a qualitative comparison by other methods such as ClusTer
Showing that the claim is valid on multiple data points instead of just one would help in making the statements stronger.

replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper892 by Reviewer 5a2j

content.title: Response to Reviewer 5a2j
content.comment:
Thanks for the valuable comments.

Answer for Weakness 1:

We neglected to analyze multiple samples to verify the effectiveness of IMR.
Due to the limitation of the length of the paper, we transferred Section 5.3 of 'Case studies and Interpretability' to Appendix A.2.

For the first conclusion in Weakness 1, we have attached other cases for interpretability and briefly explain them in Appendix A.2.

Thanks for the valuable comments on the following “conclusion”, which you thought of as a conclusion in our paper. We have attached the analysis of time distance and Path Confidence in Appendix A.3, which will help analyze datasets and verify the rationality of time negative sampling.
Nevertheless, we must affirm that this sentence is not a conclusion in our paper. This is just a common phenomenon, but it is not true at all times. The analysis in our paper is as follows.

On the one hand, the explanation given by the Path Confidence is that the reliability of paths 2-1, 2-2, 2-3, and 2-4 gradually decreases.

On the other hand, the actual time distance is gradually increasing. From empirical points of view, the attributes between entities that are closer in time are more similar, so the path reliability should be gradually reduced.

The paper supposes that the reliability of the path indicated by the Path Confidence is consistent with the actual situation, i.e., the conclusions given by the indicator are compatible with the usual experience.
However, we do not achieve the conclusion that the reliability of paths with larger time distances is lower. There exist some counterexamples in reality.
We have attached experiments to analyze the relations between time distance and Path Confidence in Appendix A.3. Experiments show that the semantic deviation of the same entity increases as the time distance increases, which verifies the rationality of time-aware negative exponentially sampling.

Answer for Weakness 2:

Considering the conclusions without adequate support, we conduct experiments on four datasets, the segmentation of which is quite different from the original. 
Besides, as the maximum hop of paths increases, the number of searching paths increases exponentially, most of which are invalid paths and weaken the performance of IMR in the paper of last version. In order to ensure that the performance of IMR does not decrease, we strictly control the number of multi-hop path samples to limit the number of multi-step paths and suppress the impact of noise samples. 
Through this operation, we can effectively suppress the performance degradation caused by adding more noise samples, which existed in the previous paper.
 In summary, the performance continues to rise with the maximum hop of paths in new experiments in Section 5.2. We conclude that IMR effectively combines multi-hop paths for reasoning.

Answer for Weakness 3:

The result of the combination of indicators are close, so attaching the standard deviation to outputs will bring difficulties to comparison and conclusions.
In order to obtain reliable conclusions, we conducted ten experiments with different random seeds and fixed hyperparameters and averaged the ten results.
Besides, we report the standard deviations in appendix A.5.

Answer for Weakness 4:

The three indicators are combined by MLP. In theory, it is equivalent to the weighted sum. When the weight for the third indicator is 0, the combination of three indicators is equivalent to the combination of the two indicators. So the performance of the three indicators should not be worse than that of the two indicators.
On new YAGO, the combination of three indicators is better than the combination of two indicators. However, on WIKI, the combination of three indicators is not entirely better the two indicators. We utilize the trained IMR to predict the training set and the test set, respectively. The performance of three indicators on the training set is better than that of two indicators (MRR:93.98%>93.84%), but the opposite is true on the test set. (MRR:80.46%<80.42%)
The phenomenon is caused by the inconsistency of the distribution between the training set and test set in WIKI. The model with three indicators is closer to the training data, causing the model to be slightly overfitting. In this way, the performance on the test set of WIKI becomes worse.

Answer for Weakness 5: 

We verify the performance of IMR on more datasets.
We adopt other reviewers' comments to experiment on four new datasets, the segmentation of which is quite different from the original.
New experiments show that IMR can always obtain the best inference performance by combining three indicators.
Because of the inconsistency between the training set and the test set in WIKI, the combination of the three indicators fits the training set better, making the performance of the three indicators not as good as that of the two indicators on the test set.

Thanks again for your careful reading and valuable comments.

display_title: Official Review of Paper892 by Reviewer hi7e

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper introduces Interpretable Multi-hop Reasoning (IMR) for temporal knowledge graph forcasting. Unlike prior work that often lacks interpretability or is unable to combine paths with different hops for reasoning, IMR can perform interpretable operations on the query and measure paths of different hops equivalently, and utilize paths with different reasoning hops. 
Specifically, IMR starts from the subject entity and finds out associate quadruples (1 hop path). Then it calculates the remaining queries for each path, and then IMR scores 1 hop path based on three indicates: query matching degree, answer completing level, and path confidence. To avoid searching space explosions it sample 1 hop path for the 2 hop path searching. Finally, it ranks the scores of all paths to obtain the preference answer. 
They conduct experiments on two large-scale datasets ICEWS and YAGO, and IMR outperforms other baselines.
content.main_review:
Strengths 
- They propose new interpretable and technically sound approaches for temporal knowledge graph reasoning. 
- Experimental results show they outperform other baselines on two widely used datasets. 

Weaknesses
- It seems that improvements from multi-hop paths are somewhat limited, especially on ICEWS. I am not sure if the authors' argument that combining different reasoning hops helps is fully justified by the experiments. 
- Given Table 3, using three indicates do not really improve the performance from other settings (e.g., best HIT@1 and HIT@3 performance come from the $f_{ac}$  $f_{qmd}$ setting) on YAGO; performance gap between "$f_{ac}$  $f_{qmd}$" and "$f_{ac}$  $f_{pc}$ $f_{qmd}$" is non significant on ICEWS as well. In my opinion, those experimental results do not support the authors' claim that combining three indicators designed by IMR can effectively measure the reasoning paths. 

Minor comments
- On Table 3 ICEWS14 HIT@3,  $f_{ac}$  $f_{qmd}$ shows 49.50 while $f_{ac}$  $f_{pc}$ $f_{qmd}$ shows 49.30 so the $f_{ac}$  $f_{qmd}$ cell should be bold.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall I think the paper introduces an interesting and technically sound approach for forecasting temporal knowledge graphs and empirically shows its competitiveness and effectiveness. However, I'm not fully convinced by some of the arguments due to the experimental results presented in Figure 2 and Table 3.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a model for temporal KG completion, i.e. prediction future links in KGs based on historical data. This paper adopts a path based approach in which starting from the query entity, it searches for the outgoing edges. Since the KG is temporal, following previous work, preference is to choose next hop which are closer in time. At each step only top-k entities are chosen based on the path scores. After each step of the hop. the queries are also updated where the entity representation is updated by a simple addition of the relation and the relation representation is updated by subtraction of the relation which was traversed. It is not clear why this update model was chosen. Also if the Trans-E formulation is chosen, the effect of the relation update cancel each other. Each path is scored by a combination of 3 scores —-(i) question matching degree, (ii) answer completing level, (iii) path confidence. I found this section very confusing and the motivation behind each of the scores was not clear to me (especially from a temporal forecasting point of view).
content.main_review:
Strengths:

1. Temporal link prediction in knowledge bases is an important problem.

Weaknesses/Questions for the authors:

1. The main weakness of the paper is currently how it is written. I personally found the writing to be very confusing and most of the model decisions were not motivated properly. Even though the paper gets good results, the paper in its current form is not ready to be accepted.
2. In equation 1, it is mentioned that an entity embedding is composed of static and dynamic components. However, it is not clear currently, how each of the components is learned.?
3. It is not clear where or how equation 2 is used?
4. What is the motivation behind eqn 3 and 4. Why is the relation embedding added to the entity representation to update it and why is it subtracted from the query embedding?
5. If we add the updated representation of entities and relations (equations 3 and 4) don't the effect of relation cancel out?
6. The scoring functions currently lack motivation. It is unclear why these scoring functions will help in temporal link prediction. 
7. In Table 2, the hits@10 of Re-Net is 65.81 which is 5 points more than the current method. Why is it not made bold in the table?
8. Please don't bold every instance of the word "path" in section 5.3. It makes reading very hard.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper introduces a model for temporal KG completion. The paper in its current form is very hard to understand. The writing and the motivation behind various modeling decisions need to be motivated much strongly. Therefore I am not recommending acceptance currently.

content.title: Response to Reviewer XtAH
content.comment:
Thanks for the valuable comments, which are of great help to our paper.

Q1.The main weakness of the paper is currently how it is written. The writing to be very confusing and most of the model decisions were not motivated properly. 

Q6. The scoring functions currently lack motivation. 

Answer for Question 1 and Question 6:

We have made significant adjustments in structure and provided motivations for all modules.
First, considering that all formula designs of IMR are based on TransE, we adjust the introduction of TransE to Section 3：Preliminary.

We attach the motivation for the Query Updating Module. We need to eliminate the semantic part that has been answered so that IMR can focus on searching the equivalent path for the unanswered parts.

For the Path Scoring Module, we attach the motivation for each indicator. We evaluate the path searching from three perspectives:

1.The searched tails should match the original question, which means that the correct tails searched by paths and the question should satisfy TransE. So IMR designs Question Matching Degree.

2.Among the paths to the correct tails, some paths are not related to the semantics of the question.  The ideal path should be the search of equivalent semantics for relations, not just for the right tails. IMR design Answer Completing Level to ensure the correctness of semantic equivalence, i.e., the path is semantically equivalent to the relation of the question.

3.Considering the particularity of the temporal KGs, the attributes of the same entity may change over time.The current sampling strategy for path searching is to sample adjacent timestamp triples of the same entity.  When the attributes of the entity changes significantly over time, it is inappropriate to perform this sampling strategy for the next hop.  It is necessary to ensure that the same entity with different timestamps has similar properties in the same path so that the searched multi-hop path is reliable. So IMR design the Path Confidence.

We have attached a detailed description of motivations in Section 4 and added Figure 2 to illustrate the indicators briefly. We also unified the description and the representation of variables in the paper.


Q2:However, it is not clear currently, how each of the components of entity embedding is learned.?

Answer for Question 2:

Based on the embedding in xERTR, IMR proposes an extra embedding component for the same entity with different timestamps. We attach the detail description of each component for entity embeddings in Appendix A.1. 

Q3:It is not clear where or how equation 2 is used?
Answer for Question 3:

Equation 2 is the modeling of triples in TransE, which is the basis of the IMR. Although this formula is not used directly, each module of IMR is based on this formula. We have adjusted this part to Section 3: Preliminary and explained its relationship with IMR in detail.


Q4:What is the motivation behind eqn 3 and 4. Why is the relation embedding added to the entity representation to update it and why is it subtracted from the query embedding?

Answer for Question 4:

TransE supposes that relations are translations between subjects and objects, that is, ${\left( {{e_s}+{r}={e_o}} \right)}$ . All indicators of IMR are designed based on TransE. So Eq 3 subtracts the relations of the path from the subject of the question to obtain the remaining subject. Eq 4 utilizes the relations of the previous question to subtract the searched relations to obtain the remaining relations for the next path search.
We attach the explanation of this design in Section 4.4.


Q5:If we add the updated representation of entities and relations (equations 3 and 4) don't the effect of relation cancel out?

Answer for Question 5:

This is a valuable question. The design of the Query Update Module should satisfy the property of offset to ensure that the question still matches the same tail entity even after the updating. This cancellation of relation guarantees that the answer to questions will not change along with paths. Only the subject of the question is applied in the calculation of Path Confidence, and only the relation in the question is used in the calculation of Answer Completing Level. This cancellation will not appear in the calculation of two indicators.
We have attached the analysis of offset to Appendix A.4.


Q7:Why is best result not made bold in the table?

Answer for Question 7:

We have rechecked the results of the experiment and bolded the best result.


Q8:Please don't bold every instance of the word "path" in section 5.3.

Answer for Question 8:

We have canceled the bolding of “path” and modified other unreasonable parts in the paper.

Thanks again for your careful reading and valuable comments, which are of great help to our paper.

content.comment:
Thanks to all the reviewers for the appreciation of our work and for making valuable recommendations. 
The previous version of the paper had many problems in writing. We have made significant adjustments in structure and content.
We have submitted an updated version of the paper based on these comments. Below is the summary of the main additions in the paper. These are complemented by the detailed responses to the individual reviewer comments.

  1. Equation 2 is the modeling of triples in TransE, which is the basis of the IMR.  We have adjusted this part to Section 3: Preliminary and explained its relationship with IMR in detail as requested by Reviewer XtAH.

  2. IMR proposes an extra embedding component for the same entity with different timestamps. We attach the detailed description of each component for entity embeddings in Appendix A.1 as requested by Reviewer XtAH.

3. We have attached a detailed description of motivations in Section 4  as requested by Reviewer XtAH and added Figure 2 to illustrate the indicators briefly.

4. We unified the description and the representation of variables as requested by Reviewer fqts. Besides, we checked and corrected the normative and consistency of other variables in the paper.

5. We conduct the experiments based on new datasets as requested by Reviewer zUEs, the segmentation of which is quite different from the original. New experiments show that IMR still achieves state-of-the-art on four baseline datasets.

6. Considering the conclusions without adequate support, we conduct comparative experiments on more datasets. In summary, we conclude that IMR effectively combines multi-hop paths for reasoning and the combination of three indicators is better than the combination of two indicators.

7. We attach new experiments to analyze the relations between time distance and Path Confidence in Appendix A.3 as requested by Reviewer 5a2j. Experiments show that the semantic deviation of the same entity increases as the time distance increases, which verifies the rationality of time-aware negative exponentially sampling.

8. The design of the Query Update Module should satisfy the property of offset to ensure that the question still matches the same tail entity even after the updating. We have attached the theoretical analysis of offset to Appendix A.4 as requested by Reviewer XtAH.

9. we have attached other cases for interpretability and briefly explain them in Appendix A.2 as requested by Reviewer 5a2j. We report the standard deviations in appendix A.5 to indicate the robustness of IMR.
